verdict: Avoid new pharma/API exposure in Haridwar for now; lend only to established, cash-generative formulation units with tight monthly monitoring, and decline new-to-bank API capex proposals.
title: Haridwar Pharmaceuticals & APIs: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**A pharma unit here buys raw materials and solvents, runs them through reactors or formulation lines, and sells to formulators, exporters or institutions on credit.** Cash sits in inventory (API and intermediates hold long) and in receivables from a handful of buyers; the rating record shows working-capital intensity of 52% in FY2019, 47% in FY2020 and 48% in 7MFY2021 at one listed peer, still described as high [10]. Pricing power is thin for generics and contract work, better for niche APIs and CDMO. **So when a proposal lands, check the buyer list and the inventory days first; if one buyer is above a third of sales, ask for the supply agreement and payment history.**

## What has changed now
**The local economy is running behind the country: Uttarakhand GST collections are -19.1% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand +4.7% against India +9.5% [D].** Nationally, output is -2.1% Apr-to-date while bank credit is +21.6% YoY, a 23.7 pp gap [D] — money is chasing a shrinking base, so weak units get refinanced rather than fixed. Locally, Akums resumed production at its Haridwar sites in May 2026 after a disruption [3], and Rishi Chemical Works has announced an API unit in the district [2]. **The local source base is thin — one awareness conference [1] and project announcements — so lean on first principles and peers, not on Haridwar-specific data.**

## Where the growth is
**Peer results show the money is in APIs and CDMO, not plain formulations: Aarti Pharmalabs posted record quarterly revenue of Rs. 613 crore, up 47% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 22.2% [4][6], and RPG Life Sciences is targeting 25% API growth [5].** The API industry grew at 8.4% CAGR between CY2017 and CY2022E and is expected at ~7% ahead, with China supplying 65-70% of India's API imports [11] — import substitution is the real demand. **Pursue established formulation units adding an API block, and CDMO suppliers to listed players; avoid new-to-bank standalone API capex and units dependent on US contract research orders, where one rating saw revenue of Rs. 61.0 crore in FY2024 hit by weak demand [8].**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the balance sheet: receivables and inventory eat cash before sales convert.** Take monthly stock and debtor statements, quarterly GST returns, and a monthly receivables-ageing; covenant a debt-service cover and a cap on single-buyer concentration. **Where a unit has fund-based limits, track utilisation — one peer's utilisation fell from 70-90% to 40-50% in Q1FY25 [9], which is the signal to ask why before it becomes a default.**

## Early-warning signs
- **GST turnover falling faster than the Uttarakhand -19.1% [D] (monthly) -> freeze new limits and inspect stock.**
- **Receivables beyond 90 days rising two months running (monthly) -> ask for buyer confirmations and shift to LC-backed sales.**
- **Power consumption per unit of output dropping (quarterly) -> check for partial shutdown; the state's demand is already +4.7% vs India +9.5% [D].**
- **Single-buyer share crossing a third of sales (quarterly) -> reprice or reduce exposure.**
watch: Turnover down more than the state's -19.1% [D] -> freeze limits, inspect stock
Over-90-day debt rising two months running -> seek buyer confirmation, move to LC sales
Utilisation stuck above 90% -> ask for the cash-flow reason before renewing
Falling while sales flat -> check for partial shutdown, reassess
Above one-third of sales -> cap exposure or reprice
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
